title: AI has inspired me to learn how to do things myself (again, but with more success)
author: ryefly
selftext:
Claude code is one of the most amazing new technologies I have ever used and I'm having a blast working on a game right now. However, trying to get my character's graphics down has been challenge. I was working with sprites initially, but I'm transitioning to a 3D character model because I want the rpg I'm making (Campy isekai story with a complex magic system and a 2.5D environment) to include a robust armor/weapon system. I also like think cel shaded graphics looks great with the environment. That being said, after attempting to work with AI to get movement down and failing constantly, I just gave up and started teaching myself how to animate, and it's been a blast! 

Claude combined with youtube vids have been great partners in my process of learning blender (relearning sort of; spent abt 100 hrs in it a few years ago) and I loooove seeing the movements I customized come to life. Moreover, I don't feel the urge to give up due to wading around in the darkness. These programs can be pretty intimidating to learn. Just putting this out there to offset much of the doomer talk about losing skills and becoming dumber. Treating Claude like a learning resource/tutor, not just a coding slave, has eliminated much of the frustration inherent in attempting to self-teach from random online resources.  \[the below is a screenshot - still a LOT to do, but I'm in no rush.\]

comments.body: Yeah, I agree. Instead of telling AI to make something for me, I've asked it to help me learn godot. Now I'm assembling it from the ground up with GPT helping me with the code elements.
